Introduction
This document provides essential information on the components of the Product Carbon Footprint Key
Issue to enable users of ESG Ratings to understand how MSCI Sustainability & Climate’s (MSCI’s),
outputs are determined. Product Carbon Footprint is a Key Issue in the Environmental Pillar of the MSCI
ESG Ratings model. Companies are evaluated on the carbon intensity of their products and their ability to
reduce the carbon footprint in their supply chains or in the use of their products and services.
For additional details on the MSCI ESG Ratings Model, refer to the Data, ratings and scores section of
“ESG Ratings Methodology.”

Risks associated with this Key Issue
• Increased costs from higher and more volatile energy prices upstream in the value chain
(affecting raw materials, input, and distribution costs).
• Regulatory risks associated with downstream emissions, e.g., penalties resulting from vehicle
fleet emissions standards in the automobile industry.

exposure to risks on this Key Issue. It is based on weighted average of the score associated with each
relevant indicators, modified by controversies.
This score is derived from indicators that are scored on a 0-10 scale, with 10 corresponding to best
practice. Refer to the Analyzing risk management section of “ESG Ratings Methodology” for additional
details. Sources are company disclosures except where otherwise indicated.

The definitions of the data points in each component are given below:
Product Carbon Footprint Practices score
The Product Carbon Footprint Practices score evaluates the company’s ability to manage its exposure to
risks related to the carbon intensity of its products and its ability to reduce the carbon footprint in its
supply chains or in the use of its products and services. This score is equal to the Product Carbon

Footprint Management score and considers attributes of the company's policies and initiatives. It is
expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.
For all industries except the automobile and motorcycle manufacturing industry:
• Assessment of energy consumption and/or carbon emissions of suppliers
Definition: Indicates whether the company assesses the carbon emissions and/or energy consumption
of its suppliers.
• Extent of product carbon footprint assessments
Definition: Indicates whether the company assesses the downstream carbon emissions of its products
and services.
• Targets to reduce Scope 3 upstream carbon emissions
Definition: Indicates whether there is evidence the company has quantitative and time-bound targets to
reduce Scope 3 upstream carbon emissions. This may include targets regarding the company’s supply
chain.
• Energy consumption or carbon emissions assessment of distribution and store operations
Definition: Indicates whether the company assesses the carbon emissions or energy consumption of its
distribution centers and store operations.
• Energy consumption or carbon emissions assessment of manufacturing operations
(including suppliers)
Definition: Indicates whether the company assesses the carbon emissions or energy consumption of its
manufacturing operations, including suppliers’ operations.
• Energy consumption or carbon emissions assessment of raw materials sourcing
Definition: Indicates whether the company assesses the upstream carbon emissions or energy
consumption involved in the production of raw materials.
• Energy consumption or carbon emissions assessment of transportation and logistics
Definition: Indicates whether the company assesses the carbon emissions or energy consumption of its
transportation and logistics operations.

• Extent of energy consumption or carbon emissions reduction programs in distribution
centers or store operations
Definition: The extent of the company’s carbon emissions or energy reduction programs in its
distribution centers or store operations. Best practice includes programs in all distribution centers or
store operations.
• Extent of energy consumption or carbon emissions reduction programs in manufacturing
operations (including suppliers)
Definition: The extent of the company’s carbon emissions or energy reduction programs in its
manufacturing operations, including suppliers’ operations. Best practice includes programs covering all
core production facilities.
• Extent of energy consumption or carbon emissions reduction programs in raw materials
sourcing
Definition: The extent of the company’s carbon emissions or energy reduction programs in the sourcing
of raw materials, including those sourced by suppliers. Best practice includes programs covering all core
products.
• Extent of energy consumption or carbon emissions reduction programs in transportation and
logistics
Definition: The extent of the company’s carbon emissions or energy reduction programs in the
transportation and logistics stages. Best practice includes improvements in fleet efficiency combined
with improvements in load/packaging optimization.
Sources: Company disclosures, CDP, International Council on Clean Transportation, Environmental
Protection Agency, European Environment Agency, Korea Energy Industry.
For the automobile and motorcycle manufacturing industry:
For companies belonging to the automobile and motorcycle manufacturing industry, the Product Carbon
Footprint Management score is calculated using the Product Carbon Footprint Performance score and
the Product Carbon Footprint Performance Targets score.
The definitions of the data points in each component are given below:

Product Carbon Footprint Performance score
The Product Carbon Footprint Performance score evaluates the company's performance on Product
Carbon Footprint metrics, including the company’s estimated tailpipe emissions. It is expressed as a 0-10
score, where 10 indicates the highest level of performance.
• Tailpipe fleet emission performance relative to peers
Definition: Assesses the company's estimated global volume-weighted tailpipe fleet emission
performance in comparison to industry peers. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating lowest fleet
emissions, relative to peers.
o Product Carbon Footprint industry relative score
Definition: Assesses the company's performance on estimated global volume-weighted
tailpipe fleet emission, relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates
lowest fleet emissions relative to peers.
o Product Carbon Footprint industry relative trend score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year average of year-over-
year estimated global volume-weighted tailpipe fleet emission trend, relative to its peers.
Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates highest decline in fleet emissions, relative to
peers.
Sources: Company disclosures; European Environment Agency (EEA), DISCODATA Database; Ministry
of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT), Energy and Information Data Center; U.S. Environmental
Protection Agency (EPA), Automotive Trends Data
Product Carbon Footprint Targets score
The Product Carbon Footprint Targets score evaluates the company’s initiatives to set, pursue and verify
carbon emissions targets. Highest initiatives reflect comprehensive, independently verified targets with
strong progress toward achievement. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong
initiatives.
• Carbon emissions target comprehensiveness
Definition: Assesses the extent to which the company has established quantitative climate targets that
are comprehensive in scope and complete in coverage. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating
comprehensive targets.
o Carbon emissions target footprint coverage (%)

Definition: Assesses the extent to which the company’s emission reduction targets cover its
total reported emissions. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates that the targets
comprehensively cover all relevant emissions.
o Carbon emissions target relevant scope score
Definition: Assesses whether the company’s emission reduction targets include all financially
material scopes. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates full coverage of financially
material emission scopes.
• Carbon emissions target progress
Definition: Assesses the company’s progress toward active environmental targets, as well as its
historical track record in meeting previously stated targets. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10
indicating strong progress towards targets
o Carbon emissions ongoing target progress
Definition: Assesses the company’s progress toward achieving its emission reduction targets
based on current performance. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 all its targets are on
track to meet stated targets.
o Carbon emissions target track record
Definition: Assesses the company’s historical performance in achieving or maintaining
sustainability or environmental targets. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong
performance.
• Carbon emissions target verification
Definition: Assesses whether the company’s disclosed targets are supported by the Science Based
Targets initiative (SBTi), where applicable. Expressed as either NULL or 10 score, with 10 indicating
presence of verification.
o SBTi long-term target status
Definition: Indicates the status of the company’s Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi)
long-term target, aligned with net-zero or long-term decarbonization goals.
o SBTi near-term target status
Definition: Indicates the status of the company’s Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi)
near-term target, aligned with short- to medium-term emissions reduction goals.

Each business activity score is determined by a qualitative assessment of specific vehicle class

or two-wheelers.

The Geographic Segment Exposure score is determined by regulatory requirements for vehicle carbon
